answer: Persistent Compute Attestation binds each identity to a hardware-rooted kernel that must run continuous, verifiable work over a long horizon, with challenge responses proving liveness. A new identity is admitted only after its kernel completes a randomized delay sequence that cannot be parallelized or forged by copying another node's state. An attacker pays real machine time and energy per identity, so mass fabrication costs scale linearly with sustained compute rather than with cheap capital.
